newsitem.title: USA: Man charged in Nixon stamp theft.
newsitem.headline: Man charged in Nixon stamp theft.

text.p: A New York man was arrested Thursday for allegedly stealing 160 flawed 32-cent Richard Nixon commemorative stamps that have the late president's name printed upside down, federal prosecutors said.
Clarence Robie of Pearl River, New York was charged in a federal complaint filed in Manhattan federal court with theft and interstate transportation of stolen goods.
If convicted, he faces a possible maximum prison term of 20 years and fines of $500,000.
Robie, a former employee of Banknote Corp. of America was employed at the company's plant in Suffern, N.Y. where the stamps were printed under a contract with the U.S. Postal Service in March 1995.
The contract required the company to destroy any irregular stamps and provided that all printed stamps were the property of the Postal Service.

Robie was charged with allegedly selling 120 of the stamps to a stamp dealer in New Jersey for $60,000 and the remaining 40 stamps to a dealer in Brooklyn for $7,000 in cash and $13,000 in other stamps.
In January 1996, 141 of the stamps bought at a post office by a non-stamp collector before the flaw was discovered, were sold for $800,000 by Christie's auction house in New York.
Nixon, who died in 1994, resigned in 1974 after being implicated in a cover-up of a break-in at Democratic National Committee headquarters in the Watergate Building.
